title: The raid's meal lasts as long as her walk, and a ransacked plot says so
tier_reason: Q-105 ruled 2026-09-11: the raid costs exactly one tomato wherever she planted, and the loss must be visible on the plot.
ask: Q-105 (b), designer 2026-09-11: 'the meal lasts as long as her walk' — the birds finish the moment she reaches the second one, so the raid costs exactly one tomato wherever she planted (near the house or ten tiles out). Sim-side and deterministic: replace RAID_EAT_SECONDS as the raid's clock with a rule read off recorded state — when the second raid bird is shooed (or comes inside her spook radius, whichever the ordinary shoo already uses), the remaining raid bird eats its tomato at once; before that, none of the three eats on a timer (a very long fallback is acceptable so a player who never goes out still loses, e.g. the ordinary EAT_SECONDS from the door if she never approaches). Keep the door as the start of the race. Update tools/measure_raid_race.gd to report the new rule (it should now print 'saves 2 of 3' on both beds), design/04 'The race, measured' and DECISION_LOG P-15's raid paragraph. Tests: both beds in the measure tool's two placements save two; replay and save/load unchanged. ALSO the designer's judgment: 'add a small animation indicator that the plot was ransacked by the bird.' Sim: mark the eaten tile with a fact (e.g. tile 'ransacked': true, cleared when she tills or plants it again; saved with the world). Presentation, first version: a small looping indicator on that tile drawn from existing effects or pixels (scattered soil, a few tumbled leaves, or the crow's feather puff repeating slowly) until the tile is worked again; wire it in world/farm.gd's draw and add an integration assertion that a ransacked tile draws it and a re-tilled tile does not. If it needs a new sprite, file that to Yuki and ship the version made from existing pixels. Keep the gateway rule and both suites green.
first_action: Read CrowBrain.raid/start_raid_meals and the eating branch in systems/sim/brains/crow_brain.gd, then write the test first: on any bed, a direct walk from the door saves two of three.
result:
Done and green. Here is what changed.

**The raid's clock is her walk now.** No raid bird eats on a count of seconds any more. The three birds are placed at dawn as before and start when she opens her front door, and the moment she has seen off the second of them, the last one takes the tomato it is standing on and goes. So the morning costs exactly one tomato whether the bed is beside the house or ten tiles out — the walk gets longer, the bill does not. The trigger is read off a bird leaving the bed, which is the same shoo report the game has always recorded, so a replay reaches the same moment from the same log.

Underneath it sits one number: the birds' patience, **a minute from the door**. That is what a player who steps outside, sees three crows on her tomatoes and does nothing loses the bed to. I picked a minute because it is far longer than any walk across the farm, so it can never be the thing that decides a race she is actually running — it is a one-line change if you want it shorter.

**The tool now plays the morning instead of reasoning about it.** `measure_raid_race.gd` walks her out onto the near bed and one ten tiles further, shoos each bird through the gateway at the tick the walk reaches it, and prints what survives. Both beds: saves 2 of 3, one tomato eaten. The unit suite calls the same two runs, so the tool and the rule cannot drift apart.

**A ransacked plot says so.** The square a bird empties now carries that fact — saved with the world, cleared the first time she works it again — and wears three clods of scattered earth that lift one after another on a slow loop. They are cut from the tilled-soil sheet the game already ships, so this cost no art; it reads clearly at 1× but it is placeholder, and a drawn mark is the one piece of this still open. Two things you should know about it: I put the mark on the *verb*, so an ordinary crow's meal marks a square too, not only the raid's three — a square something ate a plant off is the same square either way. And a ransacked square shows nothing new in the save file unless it actually has a mark, so old saves load unchanged.

Unit suite 2691 passed, integration 887 passed, robot session passed, the one-gateway check and the benchmark pass. Nothing is committed — the work is in the worktree for review.

conversation.text: Chief of staff, after the check: landed with one change of shape. The clods did not actually stir on screen — the farm only redraws while a reaction is in flight — so the mark is now its own small node (world/ransack_mark.gd) that redraws itself each frame, one per marked square, kept in step with the sim on a load, a replay and an eat action. Cost scales with marked squares, not the map. The patience comment now quotes the measured seconds.

follow_ups.title: Draw the mark a crow leaves on a plot it emptied
follow_ups.first_action: Read 'A ransacked plot says so' in docs/design/04-pests-and-ecology.md and the three-clod placeholder in world/farm.gd (RANSACK_* constants), then make a 16px looping mark for an emptied soil square — scattered soil and a few tumbled leaves or a dropped feather, 3-4 frames, in the tilled-soil palette — and say which sheet and cell the renderer should read it from.
follow_ups.why: The mark ships today as clods cut from the soil sheet, which is a placeholder the designer's ruling explicitly allowed until real art exists.

recommend.question: The plot a crow ransacks is marked with soil pixels borrowed from the ground sheet — leave it, or have a proper one drawn?
recommend.answer: Have Yuki draw it; keep the borrowed pixels on screen until hers lands.
recommend.why: It is the only thing in the whole raid a player actually looks at, and a drawn mark is one cheap sprite under the current art budget.
recommend.instead: Leave the clods and spend the art elsewhere — they do read as scuffed earth, and nobody but us knows they came off the dirt tile.

check.summary: The raid's clock is now her walk (last bird eats on the second shoo, 60 s patience under it), the tool plays both beds and asserts two saved, the ransacked tile is saved and cleared correctly, and a drawn mark is filed to Yuki — but the on-screen mark does not actually loop as the reply and design/04 say, and I could not rerun the suites myself, so the pass counts are Tomas's word until the drain's run.

findings.what: The 'slow loop' is not on screen: farm.gd's _process switches itself off whenever no reaction, refusal, ack or soak is in flight, and nothing schedules a redraw while a ransacked tile exists, so the clods only shift when something else happens to redraw. The integration test asserts the pure function at two times, not that the screen animates — the same 'measured the wrong step' shape as the pilot
findings.where: world/farm.gd:1160 (_process early exit) and the new ransack_marks/_draw block
findings.fix: Keep processing on while any tile is marked (a count of ransacked tiles from the sim in the early-exit condition, so cost scales with marked tiles, not map area), or drop the 'loop' wording from the doc and reply and ship it as a static mark. Then make the scenario assert the redraw path, not just ransack_clods.

findings.what: Comment overstates the margin: it says the farthest bed the tool finds is reached in 'about a fifth' of the 60 s patience; from the recorded times the far bed's last bird is ~7 s from the door, nearer an eighth. The conclusion (patience can never decide a real race) still holds.
findings.fix: Say 'well under a fifth' or quote the measured seconds.

findings.what: Suite results are unverified by me: the sandbox refused to run godot and the gateway checker here, so 'unit 2691 / integration 887 / robot session passed' is the worker's claim. The drain reruns both suites on landing; treat that run as the evidence.
findings.fix: Read the drain's suite output before committing; no action if green.
